items.title: 61530_Roy Eldridge oral history interview
items.q: Because they had five Black musicians: Teddy Wilson, Specs Powell, Casey, Al Hall and myself.

ctx.x: No, I was busy tootin'... You see, with me, I was too busy trying to play. You know, and I'd prepare myself for the things I would eventually get to, and I did... But then what I got to was such a farce, man, you know...! I mean, you think you go through life trying to get yourself straight, and you reach a goal, and there's still a fence out there. See, that's what hurts. See, I think that's what just turned me off completely, or else I would have been able to play better than I was playing, you know.

We did this gig the other day, and they drop all the heavy work on you, you know. Things you think you're going to get to, you don't get, you know. You only get like the one show. While you're doing that one show, they're picketing the place. It's pretty wild in New York City, ain't it? Because they had five Black musicians: Teddy Wilson, Specs Powell, Casey, Al Hall and myself. And because they had those five cats in there, the White musicians didn't dig it, man.
So who was picketing? The musicians?
